strings.name: James Gosling
strings.summary: James Gosling led Java's early language design at Sun, working with a team on running programs across hardware platforms. His earlier projects included editors, Unix and virtual machines; Java grew from consumer-electronics research into network software. The language, virtual machine and development ecosystem influenced enterprise computing and education. After Sun, he also worked on ocean robotics and cloud engineering.
strings.coverageNote: Research checked through 13 November 2026; selected milestones extend to 2024. This is not a daily news archive. Shared achievements are credited to collaborators and teams.
strings.influence.rationale: Helped create the Java language and runtime platform, advancing the long-term development of cross-platform applications and enterprise software.

strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-2.value: University of Calgary computer-science bachelor's (1977); Carnegie Mellon PhD (1983)
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Java and its virtual machine
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Worked with Sun colleagues on Java and a virtual-machine architecture for portable programs.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Systems engineering
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Worked on editors and window systems, later applying software engineering to autonomous ocean robots and cloud services.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Announced retirement
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Publicly announced retirement after engineering work at Amazon.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Computer History Museum fellow
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Recognized for the conception, design and implementation of Java.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Joined AWS
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Became an AWS distinguished engineer, moving into cloud-related engineering.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Left Sun and Oracle
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Left after Oracle acquired Sun, then worked briefly at Google and joined Liquid Robotics.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Java introduced publicly
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Sun launched Java, taking the former consumer-device project toward networked, portable applications.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Green project began
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Worked with Mike Sheridan and Patrick Naughton on the project that developed Oak, later renamed Java.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Carnegie Mellon doctorate
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Completed his computer-science doctorate after work on Unix Emacs and multiprocessor software.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Calgary degree
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Received a computer-science bachelor's degree before graduate study in the United States.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Born in Calgary
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Born in Calgary; he states the date and place in his recorded oral history.
